settings.heading: What we won't stock, and why.
settings.text: A growing list of ingredients we prohibit or restrict, with plain explanations of the science and the reasoning. Jump by letter or search by name.
settings.detail_text: A skin-lightening agent. In many regions it is prescription-only because of irritation and long-term safety concerns, so we keep it out of over-the-counter formulas entirely.

settings.name: Aluminum powder
settings.detail: Metallic pigment; restricted by purity and inhalation concerns

settings.name: Formaldehyde
settings.detail: Preservative and releasers; prohibited for irritation and cancer risk

settings.name: Hydroquinone
settings.detail: Skin-lightening agent; prescription-only in many places

settings.name: Parabens
settings.detail: Preservatives; limited to short-chain types at low levels

settings.name: Talc
settings.detail: Mineral powder; allowed only with proof of asbestos-free testing

settings.heading: Why an ingredient lands on the list

settings.title: Human health
settings.text: Evidence of harm to people at the doses found in cosmetics.

settings.title: Environmental health
settings.text: Persistence or harm to wildlife and water systems.

settings.title: Sustainability
settings.text: Sourcing that strips land, water or biodiversity.

settings.title: Ethics
settings.text: Links to forced labor or other human-rights abuses in supply chains.

settings.title: Expert judgment
settings.text: A call made by our science team when the data is mixed.

settings.heading: Four things we weigh before deciding

settings.title: The research
settings.text: Peer-reviewed studies, weighed for quality rather than counted.

settings.title: Regulators
settings.text: Agencies often disagree, so we read their reasoning, not just their verdicts.

settings.title: Real exposure
settings.text: How much of it touches skin or is breathed in, and how often.

settings.title: Safer swaps
settings.text: We check the replacement isn't worse before asking brands to switch.
